subject: BrightWorks MSA & Order Form — output ownership and training carveouts
body:
From: Simon Park <simon.park@brightworks.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@brightworks.com, procurement@brightworks.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: MSA + Order Form — IP carveouts & training clause

Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and a proposed order form. High level asks: BrightWorks must retain exclusive ownership of outputs generated from our proprietary data sets (we label this as "Customer Content"), and we require an explicit carveout that prevents Redwood from using Customer Content to train or improve models.

We are OK with a narrow feedback license for aggregated, anonymized telemetry but need an option to opt-out at the project level. For commercial clarity, we also called out attribution and downstream productization restrictions (no resale of outputs that include BrightWorks proprietary content).

Please confirm teams to loop in on legal and procurement. We need a final MSA by end of next week to meet our FY procurement cycle.

Attachments: BrightWorks_MSA_redlines_20280110.pdf, BW-OrderForm-Quote-20280110.xlsx

Regards,
Simon Park
Head of Procurement, BrightWorks, Inc.
Simon.Park@brightworks.com

----

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Simon Park <simon.park@brightworks.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: MSA + Order Form — IP carveouts & training clause

Simon — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. We reviewed the redlines with product and legal. Quick responses up front:

- Output ownership: we understand the need for BrightWorks to control outputs that are solely derived from your Customer Content. Our standard approach is to grant customers title to "Customer Outputs" while retaining rights to model-level improvements. Can you confirm the types of outputs you are most concerned about (e.g., model-exportable artifacts, bulk export of generated datasets, derived customer-facing features)?

- Training carveout: Redwood is open to a Customer Content carveout that prevents us from incorporating Customer Content into training corpora used for commercial models. We typically express that as: "Customer Content will not be used to retrain or improve Redwood-hosted models without explicit opt-in." Would BrightWorks accept an explicit opt-in mechanism per project plus an initial opt-out by default?

- Feedback license: product team prefers a limited license to use aggregated and anonymized telemetry for service quality and safety improvements. We can add a project-level toggle and 30-day rolling window for retention if that helps.

Can you confirm whether procurement expects an indemnity or escrow clause tied to model drift/productization? Laura — looping you for legal redline direction. Ben — can you estimate impact to our offering if we add project opt-outs (routing/segregation work)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to push to final.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

----

From: Simon Park <simon.park@brightworks.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@brightworks.com, procurement@brightworks.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: MSA + Order Form — IP carveouts & training clause

Neha — appreciate the quick reply. Clarifications:

- By "outputs" we mean both (1) generated artifacts returned to users (text, images, structured data) and (2) any derivative datasets we export or embed into our product. We are OK if Redwood retains model-level improvements that are strictly statistical (i.e., not our proprietary phrasing).

- Training carveout: procurement insists on an explicit prohibition: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train models for any purpose unless BrightWorks provides written consent via a signed addendum." The opt-in mechanism is acceptable, but procurement wants the default to be opt-out.

- Feedback: BrightWorks accepts aggregated telemetry for safety fixes but requires (a) an opt-out option, (b) a 30-day maximum retention for raw logs containing Customer IDs, and (c) proof of anonymization practices.

Also tagging our legal counsel — we are evaluating a modest escrow arrangement for models that are customized on our data and will share a draft escrow schedule.

Simon Park
Head of Procurement, BrightWorks, Inc.

----

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Simon Park <simon.park@brightworks.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: MSA + Order Form — output ownership and training carveouts

Simon — thanks. We can work toward a compromise that should be acceptable to procurement while preserving our ability to improve the service. Proposed pathway:

1) Output ownership: add "Customer Output" definition that covers user-visible generated artifacts and exported derivative datasets. Redwood will assign title to BrightWorks for Customer Outputs where the output is materially derived from Customer Content. We will exclude model checkpoints, model weights, and aggregated statistical features.

2) Training prohibition: accept a firm default opt-out: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or improve any models without BrightWorks' prior written consent." We will add operational language describing the opt-in process (signed addendum per project) and an audit record. This will require a small implementation to tag and route opt-in corpora; estimate 2 sprints of infra work.

3) Feedback and telemetry: agree to a constrained feedback license limited to aggregated, anonymized metrics for safety/performance. Allow a project-level opt-out and commit to a maximum 30-day retention for logs containing Customer IDs; provide a SOC2-style summary of the anonymization process in writing.

Next steps: Laura, can legal prepare the MSA clause language based on the bullets above? Simon — if procurement can sign the order form (price) into DocuSign we can finalise MSA language in parallel and target sign-off by 2028-01-19.

DocuSign (order form): https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ABCDEF123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
